note: Fits commercially and on starting point, and fails the exclusion on the half nobody measures. He owns his own business and travels for it, which satisfies 'successful'; he registered $6,000 as significant ('a lot of money, a lot of money') but never as unaffordable, and nothing suggests he cannot pay, so income holds. Neglected health is the criterion he embodies most exactly — it took a hospital admission at his heaviest ever weight to make health a priority at all. Good-to-great is the interesting one: eight months ago he would have failed it outright, but he arrives at 158 lb and 17.7% body fat having self-rescued 47 lb, and what he is buying now is muscle and a six-pack, not weight loss. He moved himself into the ICP before the call. The miss is 'not deconditioned', and it is the exact mirror of the John Viola case in this same batch: Viola is at the excluded weight but loves training, while this prospect is at a healthy weight and is genuinely gym-averse — 'the thought of working out makes me want to puke' and 'I haven't lifted a finger in months.' The stated criterion bundles body composition and attitude into a single test, and two prospects in one batch each fail exactly one half of it. That bundling is the finding, not the individual verdict.
